intended_object: The scalar extension K ⊗_R M of a topological R-module M along a finite field extension K/R (both fields discrete), seen as a topological R-module (its "base-linear" view). The tensor product carries the finest module topology that makes every map m ↦ c ⊗ m continuous. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the surrounding `FiniteFieldSpecialization` section.
explanation:
The body is just `discreteExtendScalarsRObj R K M`, which is `tensorLeftObj R (coefficient R K) M`. Its carrier is `TensorProduct R K M`, where `K` has the R-module structure coming from the algebra map. Its topology is the finest topological-module topology making each map m ↦ c ⊗ₜ m continuous. When K is discrete, this is the standard topology on the scalar extension of a topological module, so the object is correct.

On generality: the extra hypotheses (`Field R`, `Field K`, `FiniteDimensional R K`, the discrete topologies) are not used by the body. The general construction, `discreteExtendScalarsRObj` for a commutative ring R and any R-algebra K, is defined in the same file, and this declaration is labelled as its specialization: the docstring says "finite-dimensional discrete-field scalar extension", and the theorem `unitContinuous_eq_discreteUnit` sits right next to it.

So this is not a construction that is only written out in a narrow setting. It is a convenience alias for the finite-field setting, and the library also has the general version. Mathlib has the purely algebraic `ModuleCat.extendScalars` for commutative algebras, but no topological-module version of this R-view. The definition therefore faithfully gives the object its docstring describes.
